title: Like spicules in silica and calcite show form is set by external forces, not chemistry

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Like spicules in silica and calcite show form is set by external forces, not chemistry

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Holothurian spicules of calcium carbonate reproduce, often indistinguishably, the forms of siliceous sponge spicules, which shows that such spicule forms are determined by the external forces acting during growth (cell confinement), not by the chemical nature or molecular structure of the material.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the Holothurian spicules are composed of calcium carbonate while those which we have just described in the case of sponges are usually, if not always, siliceous: this being just another proof of the fact that in such cases the form of the spicule is not due to its chemical nature or molecular structure, but to the external forces

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Spicules confined to a cell surface”. Scope: sponge and holothurian spicules

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The morphological premise is testable with existing specimens and images. The conclusion that chemistry is irrelevant and confinement causal is weakly discriminated by morphology alone, so only part of the claim can be resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Extract quantitative shape descriptors for siliceous sponge and calcitic holothurian spicules and test convergence after controlling for developmental compartment geometry. Similar shapes across materials support material-independence only if within-material and cell-confinement alternatives are modeled.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Similarity across materials does not by itself identify the shaping force.

Comparable developmental cell geometry is generally absent.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.6
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Form overlap versus mineral class is a fair empirical reading of the argument, and both spicule faunas are extensively illustrated. The illustrations are not a joint morphometric dataset, and holothurian and sponge images sit in different literatures. Similar shapes would still be compatible with convergence for reasons other than cell confinement, so the chemistry-independence claim is only partly separated from its rivals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Embed siliceous sponge spicules and calcareous holothurian spicules in a common morphospace and test whether corresponding forms overlap. Overlap supports form set by shared external confinement; separation that tracks mineralogy rather than shape class would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The two groups are not a controlled contrast: cell geometry and ancestry differ along with chemistry.

Quantitative spicule outlines are not in one downloadable table and would have to be measured from plates.
